title: Joint ERT and seismic refraction: structure-constrained water content
caveat: Cached output of an offline run (no API key, no LLM call) of PyHydroGeophysX 0.5.0 on data shipped in examples/data. It is not a result for your data.
summary: Request: "Invert the ERT line with the seismic refraction structure and estimate the water content". The run finished with status 'success' in 122 s: Load ERT data -> Run ERT inversion -> Evaluate inversion quality -> Run seismic refraction inversion -> Extract structural constraints -> Convert to water content -> Fuse methods -> Generate report.

figures.label: Resistivity, constrained by the 1200 m/s velocity interface

steps: [done] load_ert_surveys -> Loaded 1 ERT survey(s) from 1 configured file(s).
[done] invert_ert -> Recovered a resistivity model from one survey.

[done] evaluate_inversion -> Quality 34.0/100 after 3 attempt(s): Quality optimization stopped after 3 attempts with score 34.0; one or more quality criteria were not met. The run now uses the best-scoring retry's model (lambda 10), up from 32.0 on the first attempt.
[done] invert_seismic -> Recovered a seismic velocity model from 357 travel times. Velocity 304 to 2682 m/s.

[done] derive_structure -> Re-inverted the first ERT survey with the 1200 m/s velocity interface built into the mesh. That model replaces the unconstrained one for the water content, the report and the exported model.

[done] convert_water_content -> Converted 1 of 1 the structure-constrained model(s) to water content by Monte Carlo petrophysics. Using 2 geological layers from the mesh markers (cells per layer: 2423, 2073).

[done] fuse_methods -> Fused seismic, ert, petrophysics (full_integration): the 1200 m/s seismic velocity interface constrained the ERT inversion; water content was converted from the structure-constrained model (Using 2 geological layers from the mesh markers (cells per layer: 2423, 2073)).
[done] write_report -> Wrote the report and its figures.
warnings: The exported model carries no layer markers: The cell markers do not describe geological structure (1356 markers for 1356 cells), so the section is treated as a single unit with one petrophysical parameter set. Supplying a layered model is what would let parameters vary with depth.
